\caption{\textbf{Smaller expansions can outperform dense connectivity.} Common observed test histories, all declared policies and both training arms. N: native; R: random; S: speed; Q: preceding-observed-base risk; V: relative-velocity RMS; D: dense. WaterDrop omits V. Symbols show seeds 0--2, short bars their mean, and dashed lines the native mean. Brackets group policies by categorical fractions of added messages, with native messages retained; this is not an empirical total-edge axis. Goop and Sand use 150 histories from 30 sources per model; WaterDrop uses 297 from 27.}
\label{fig:observed-accuracy-budget}
\end{figure*}
